title: Denmark – Construction work – Slamafvanding ME.04
description: Kalundborg Central Renseanlæg (herefter ”KCR”) skal udvides som en konsekvens af, at industrien i Kalundborg Kommune i de kommende år forøger sin tilledning. Udvidelsen af KCR (herefter ”Projektet”) sker både for at øge den biologiske kapacitet af anlægget, bedre styring af overløb, ny slamafvanding og fjernelse af miljøfremmede stoffer gennem tredje og fjerde renseanlæg. Projektet realiseres gennem en række udbud inden for byggeri- og anlæg, maskin- og el, systemleverandører og SRO. Kalundborg Renseanlæg A/S (”Bygherre”) har indgået en totalrådgiveraftale med Envidan A/S, som forestår teknisk rådgivning og bistand, projektering, byggeledelse og processpecialistrådgivning i forbindelse med Projektets realisering. Dette udbud omfatter en hovedentreprisekontrakt, som i hovedtræk indebærer udførelse af følgende arbejder: • Slamafvanding • Polymeranlæg • Transportøranlæg • Containerløsning for afvandet slam • Slampumper • Slamlagertank • Anlæg for teknisk vand • Trykluftanlæg • Biofilter (luftrensning) • El- og SRO-anlæg for ovenstående Bygningsarbejderne forbundet med at realisere procestrinene udbydes i et særskilt udbud. Tilbudsgiverne skal i tilbudslisten prissætte variable ydelser, herunder reguleringspriser, som kommer til anvendelse, i det omfang, der er behov for. Bygherre har overvejet, om indkøbet kan opdeles yderligere, men vurderer, at en yderligere opdeling vil indebære en række uhensigtsmæssige tekniske og juridiske grænseflader med deraf følgende risiko for forhindringer i udførelsesfasen samt afledte transaktionsomkostninger.

title: Netherlands – Accounting, auditing and fiscal services – (Heraanbesteding) Europese aanbesteding Fiscale adviesdiensten Gemeente Breda
description: Procedure Aanbesteding middels de Europees openbare procedure conform de (gewijzigde) aanbestedingswet 2012. Opdrachtgever De opdrachtgever bij deze aanbesteding is de Gemeente Breda. Voor meer informatie over de Gemeente Breda verwijzen wij u naar de website van de gemeente: www.breda.nl. Opdracht De opdracht betreft een raamovereenkomst voor integrale fiscale adviesdiensten. De fiscale adviesdiensten hebben betrekking op alle mogelijke fiscale vraagstukken bij de gemeentelijke overheid of gelieerde overheidsbedrijven of deelnemingen, waaronder in ieder geval op het gebied van: - Vennootschapsbelasting; - Omzetbelasting (incuslief BTW compensatiefonds); - Loonbelasting; - Overdrachtsbelasting. Opdrachtgever heeft een fiscaal team binnen de organisatie welke voorziet in de fiscale advisering van de organisatie. Dit team heeft de fiscale (basis) kennis in huis en zorgt voor voorbereiding van aangiften. Het doel van deze raamovereenkomst is ondersteuning van het fiscaal team op het gebied van: - Indienen aangiften vennootschapsbelasting; - Uitvoeren van een jaarlijkse steekproefrapportage; - Natuurlijke adviesfunctie: sparringpartnerfunctie in (complexe) adviesvragen; - Back up in geval van te grote werkvoorraad. Jaarlijks wordt van opdrachtnemer gevraagd om in ieder geval de aangifte vennootschapsbelasting in te dienen. Voor het overige geeft de aanbestedende dienst geen omzetgarantie. Het daadwerkelijk benodigde fiscaal advies is voor een belangrijk deel afhankelijk van politieke, economische, maatschappelijke en interne ontwikkelingen. Voor de overige werkzaamheden zal voorafgaand aan de uitvoering van de werkzaamheden de inschrijver op verzoek van de gemeente een offerte/kostenraming indienen. Percelen Deze opdracht is niet verdeeld in percelen. Maximale contractwaarde De maximale opdrachtwaarde in het kader van deze raamovereenkomst wordt gesteld op € 240.000,- bezien over de looptijd van de overeenkomst, inclusief verlengingsopties. Aan het genoemde bedrag kunnen geen rechten worden ontleend. Voor opdrachtgever geldt geen afnameverplichting. Mocht gedurende de looptijd van de raamovereenkomst de maximale opdrachtwaarde worden overschreden dan zal de raamovereenkomst (eerder) worden beëindigd. Mercell Deze aanbesteding zal uitsluitend en geheel digitaal online worden afgehandeld via het Mercell platform (www.mercell.com). Een uitgebreide instructie met betrekking tot digitaal aanbesteden treft u aan in de Vragenlijsten.

description: Hankinnan kohteena on kahden uniikin (tarjottuja leikkivälineitä ei ole toimitettu muualle) leikkivälineen toimittaminen asennettuna Lappeenrannan kaupungille. Hankittavat leikkivälineet tulevat Lappeenrantaan satama-alueelle. Ensimmäisen leikkivälineen teemana on "Hevonen" ja toisen leikkivälineen teemana on "Linna". Välineiden tulee mahtua kaikkine rakenneosineen ja putoamisalustoineen tarjouspyynnössä esitetyille tilavarausalueille. Tarjouspyynnöllä haetaan kahta uniikkia, ympäristöön sopivaa ja eri ikäryhmät huomioivia leikkivälinettä. Leikkivälineiden tulee olla myös keskenään yhteensopivia ulkonäöltään. Kilpailutus tehdään käänteisenä kilpailutuksena, eli ranskalaisena urakkana. Käänteisessä kilpailutuksessa hankinnan enimmäishinta on määritelty etukäteen, eli hinnoilla ei kilpailla. Tästä tulee myös termi kiinteähintainen kilpailutus. Tarjoajat siis kilpailevat yksinomaan laatutekijöillä. Hankintaa ei jaeta osiin. Tarjoajan on tarjottava molemmat leikkivälineet. Hankinnan arvo on 280 000 euroa (alv 0%). Sopimuskausi alkaa mahdollisimman pian hankintapäätöksen saatua lainvoiman. Sopimus alkaa aikaisintaan, kun molemmat osapuolet ovat allekirjoittaneet sopimuksen. Sopimus on voimassa siihen asti, kunnes leikkivälineet ovat hyväksytysti toimitettu sekä asennettu ja hyväksytysti käyttöönotettu tilaajan määrittämiin kohteisiin.

title: Finland – Health and social work services – KUNTOUTUSTUKEA SAAVAN NUOREN AMMATILLINEN VALMENNUS, Pohjois-Suomi
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Kansaneläkelaitoksen (Kelan) henkilöasiakkaille järjestettävä kuntoutuspalvelu, Kuntoutustukea saavan nuoren ammatillinen valmennus, ja sen kehittäminen. Tämä tarjouspyyntö koskee Pohjois-Suomen alueelle kilpailutettavaa palvelua. Hankittava palvelu on osa Kuntoutustukea saavien kuntoutuksen kehittämisprojektia, joka toteutetaan vuosina 2025-2028. Projektissa luodaan uusi yksilöllinen ammatillinen kuntoutuspalvelu asiakkaille, jotka saavat kuntoutustukea ainoastaan Kelasta. Kuntoutustukea saavan nuoren ammatillisen valmennuksen kohderyhmänä on 18-29 -vuotias asiakas, jonka sairaus tai vamma on aiheuttanut tai sen arvioidaan aiheuttavan lähivuosina asiakkaan työ- tai opiskelukyvyn ja ansiomahdollisuuksien olennaisen heikentymisen Kelan kuntoutuslain 6 § mukaisesti (Kansaneläkelaitoksen kuntoutusetuuksista ja kuntoutusrahaetuuksista annettu laki 566/2005). Asiakkaalle on myönnetty Kelan maksama kuntoutustuki, jota asiakas on saanut alle 2 vuotta. Asiakkaan työ- ja toimintakyvyn on arvioitu palautuvan asianmukaisella hoidolla ja/tai kuntoutuksella. Valmennuksen tavoitteena on aktivoida asiakasta siirtymään kuntoutustuelta opintoihin, työelämään tai muihin kuntoutuspalveluihin. Kuntoutustukea saavan nuoren ammatillinen valmennus toteutetaan yksilökuntoutuksena. Valmennuksen toteuttaa valmentaja ja se sisältää sekä kasvokkaista kuntoutusta että etäkuntoutusta. Palvelu sisältää tapaamisia, joista osa voidaan toteuttaa kuvapuheluina, lisäksi palveluun sisältyy verkkokuntoutusta sekä verkostotyötä. Palvelu toteutetaan seuraavan palvelukuvauksen mukaisesti (voimassa 1.4.2027 alkaen): - Kuntoutustukea saavan nuoren ammatillinen valmennus, Kasvokkaisen ja etäkuntoutuksen yhdistelmä. Kelan kuntoutuksen palvelukuvauksessa ja siihen kuuluvissa liitteissä (1-4) määritellään Kelan järjestämän kuntoutuksen sisältö ja sen laatuvaatimukset. title: Finland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Rakentamisen suunnittelupalvelut
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Koulutuskuntayhtymä OSAOn rakentamisen suunnittelupalvelut. Sopimuskausi on kaksi (2) vuotta, minkä jälkeen on mahdollisuus kahteen (2) yhden (1) vuoden optioon. Puitejärjestelyn ennakoitu arvonlisäveroton arvo sekä puitejärjestelyn enimmäisarvo koko sopimuskaudella on 2 000 000 euroa. Hankinta on jaettu yhdeksään (9) osa-alueeseen. Hankinnasta on järjestetty markkinavuoropuhelu 9.6.2026 klo 12.00. Markkinavuoropuhelusta oli tehty ilmoitus Hilmaan 12.5.-8.6.2026 väliseksi ajaksi ja kaikilla kiinnostuneilla oli mahdollisuus osallistua markkinavuoropuheluun. Markkinavuoropuhelussa mietittiin tulevan puitejärjestelyn toimintamallia ja laatuvaatimuksia sekä esiteltiin OSAOn kiinteistöjä, joihin palvelu kohdistuu. Toimittajilla oli mahdollisuus myös esittää kysymyksiä tulevaa hankintaa koskien. Kilpailutusmateriaalit lähetettiin markkinavuoropuheluun osallistuneille kommentoitavaksi 13.10-20.10.2026 väliseksi ajaksi. Tällä sopimuksella hankitaan olemassa oleviin rakennuksiin tarvittavaa suunnittelupalvelua. Tilaajalla on kuitenkin halutessaan mahdollisuus hankkia myös uudisrakennuksia koskevia suunnittelupalveluita tämän puitesopimuksen sisältä. Tilaaja voi kilpailuttaa erillisenä hankintana suunnittelupalvelut niissä rakennushankkeissa, joiden kokonaisarvo ylittää 350 000 euroa ja jotka käsitellään Koulutuskuntayhtymä OSAOn talousarviossa suurina rakennushankkeina. Tämän sopimuksen mukaisilla toimittajilla on mahdollisuus osallistua myös näihin kilpailutuksiin. Puitesopimus ei sisällä asemakaavoitukseen, asemakaavan muutoksiin tai muihin maankäytön suunnittelutehtäviin liittyviä palveluita. Tilaaja hankkii nämä palvelut erikseen. Puitejärjestelyllä hankitaan palveluita hankintatarpeen ilmetessä. Puitesopimus ei sisällä määräostovelvoitetta Tilaajalle. Kaikki palvelun ostomääristä annetut arviot ovat alustavia arvioita, eivätkä sido Tilaajaa.

description: Het betreft hier een raamovereenkomst voor het groot-, klein- en levensverlengend asfaltonderhoud binnen de gemeente Hof van Twente. title: Finland – Works for complete or part construction and civil engineering work – Mikkelin kaupungin kunnallisteknisten -, viherrakennus- ja metsänhoitotöiden puitejärjestely 2027- 2029 (optio 2 vuotta)
description: Mikkelin kaupungin kunnallisteknisten -, viherrakennus- ja metsänhoitotöiden puitejärjestely 2027-2029 (optio 2 vuotta) hankinta koskee urakointia pääsääntöisesti keskeisellä kaupunkialueella, mutta myös Anttolassa, Haukivuorella, Ristiinassa, Otavassa ja Suomenniemellä. Puitejärjestelysopimuksen kesto on 2 vuotta (1.2.2027-31.1.2029, optiovuodet 1.2.2029-31.1.2031). Sopimuskausi alkaa 1.2.2027 sopimuksen allekirjoittamisen jälkeen. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvo ylittää rakennusurakoiden EU-kynnysarvon 5 404 000 euroa (alv. 0 %). Puitejärjestelyyn valitaan osa-alueittain 3-8 urakoitsijaa, jotka täyttävät soveltuvuusvaatimukset, kelpoisuusehdot ja ovat antaneet hyväksyttävät tarjoukset. Tilaaja hankkii sopimuskauden aikana osa-alueittain valituilta urakoitsijoilta urakoita ja niihin liittyviä palveluja tarjouspyynnössä ja sopimuksessa määritellyin ehdoin. Urakoitsija toimii puitesopimuksen mukaisilla kohteilla päätoteuttajana. Hankintaa koskevat työt ovat yksilöimättömiä. Tämän hankintaprosessin perusteella valitaan kuhunkin osa-alueeseen ne puitetoimittajat, joiden kanssa tehdään puitesopimus. Urakoitsijoiden määrä, valintaperusteet, puitejärjestely toimintamalli ja tilausmenettely on kuvattu tarkemmin osa-alueittain. Puitejärjestely on jaettu kuuteen (6) osa-alueeseen: 1. Osa-alue: Vaativat infrarakennustyöt 2. Osa-alue: Infrarakennustyöt 3. Osa-alue: Viheralueiden ja leikkipaikkojen rakennustyöt 4. Osa-alue: Pilaantuneen maan kunnostustyöt 5. Osa-alue: Metsänhoitotyöt 6. Osa-alue: Metsäkonetyöt Tarjouksen voi jättää yhdestä tai useammasta osa-alueesta. Hankintapäätökset tehdään osa-alueittain. Puitetoimittajan kanssa tehdään yksi (1) sopimus riippumatta siitä, kuinka moneen osa-alueeseen on tullut valituksi. Puitetoimittajan ja tilaajan välinen kommunikointi tapahtuu suomen kielellä. Puitetoimittajan edustajan, vastaavan työnjohtajan ja vähintään yhden (1) työntekijän jokaisesta työryhmästä on kyettävä kommunikoimaan sekä suullisesti että kirjallisesti suomen kielellä. Kuhunkin osa-alueeseen valitaan tarjouspyynnön ja liitteenä olevien dokumenttien mukaisesti tilaajan tarpeita vastaava määrä puitetoimittajia, jotka täyttävät tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaiset kelpoisuusehdot ja joiden tarjoukset ovat hyväksyttäviä. Osa-alueittain sopimuksia tehdään vastaavasti vähemmän, mikäli hyväksyttäviä tarjouksia saadaan vähemmän. Kestävän kehityksen edistämiseksi tämän puitesopimuksen työmailla vähimmäisvaatimus kaluston Euro-päästöluokituksissa on kuorma-autojen osalta Euro V sekä massaltaan yli 15 tonnia painavien kaivinkoneiden ja metsänhoitokoneiden osalta Stage IV. Kuorma-autojen päästöluokitusvaatimus ei koske koneiden siirtoon käytettävää kalustoa, eikä yksittäisiä kappaletavarakuljetuksia. Tilaaja voi järjestää puitejärjestelyn sisäisiä kilpailutuksia (minikilpailutuksia) puitejärjestelyyn valittujen urakoitsijoiden kesken. Urakoitsija voi tapauskohtaisesti päättää osallistumisestaan minikilpailutukseen. Urakoitsijalla ei ole velvollisuutta jättää tarjousta puitejärjestelyn perusteella järjestettävissä minikilpailutuksissa. Kaupunki voi myös kilpailuttaa tämän puitejärjestelyn ulkopuolella kohteet, joissa aikataulu ja suunnitelmavalmius sen mahdollistavat. Tilaaja päättää hankekohtaisesti, mihin osa-alueeseen kilpailutettavat urakat kuuluvat. Puitejärjestely ei anna urakoitsijalle yksinoikeutta hankinnan kohteena olevien urakoiden toteuttamiseen tai palveluiden tuottamiseen. Tilaaja pidättää itsellään oikeuden hylätä perustellusta syystä kaikki tehdyt tarjoukset. Mikkelin kaupungin muut yksiköt sekä kaupunkikonserniyhtiöt voivat hyödyntää puitejärjestelyä. Kohteissa, joissa rakentamiseen kuuluu asfaltointia, päällystystyöt voidaan toteuttaa pääurakkaan alistettuna sivu-urakkana. Sivu-urakan alistamisesta tehdään hanke kohtainen alistamissopimus, jonka allekirjoittavat tilaaja, pääurakoitsija sekä sivu-urakoitsija. Alistamissopimuksella pääurakoitsija velvoitetaan huolehtimaan siitä, että alistettu sivu-urakoitsija suorittaa työnsä omien urakkasopimustensa ja alistamissopimuksen mukaisessa järjestyksessä alistamissopimuksen yhteisesti laaditun aikataulun mukaisesti. Alistaminen asettaa pääurakoitsijalle vain aikatauluun ja työjärjestykseen liittyviä velvoitteita. Päällystysurakoitsija laskuttaa asfaltoinnin osalta tilaajaa heidän keskinäisen sopimuksen mukaisilla hinnoilla. Kaupunki voi myös teetättää asfaltoinnin omana työnään.

title: Finland – Financial auditing services – Kouvolan kaupunkikonsernin tilintarkastuspalvelut vuosille 2027 - 2030 (+ 2 optiovuotta 2031 - 2032)
description: Tarjous annetaan Kouvolan kaupunkikonserniin kuuluvien kaupungin ja sen tytäryhteisöjen tilivuosien 2027 - 2030 (+ 2 optiovuotta 2031 - 2032, jos tilaaja niin päättää) tilintarkastuspalveluista. Tilaaja ilmoittaa option käyttämisestä toimittajalle kirjallisesti viimeistään kolme (3) kuukautta ennen varsinaisen sopimuskauden päättymistä. Tarjous pyydetään kuntalain (410/2015) 122 §:n mukaisesta hallinnon ja talouden tarkastuksesta tilikausia 2027 - 2030 vastaavilta vuosilta ja EU- ja muiden hankkeiden tilintarkastuksesta sekä muista tilintarkastusta tukevista asiantuntijapalveluista tämän tarjouspyynnön mukaisesti. Tarjouspyynnön kohteena ovat tilintarkastuslain (1141/2015) ja julkishallinnon ja talouden tilintilintarkastuksesta annetun lain (1142/2015) mukainen rekisteröity tilintarkastusyhteisö. Tarjouskilpailun järjestää Kouvolan kaupungin tarkastuslautakunta. Tarkastuslautakunnan toiminta tarjouskilpailun järjestäjänä kaupunkikonsernin puolesta perustuu kuntalakiin (410/2015). Kuntalain 122 § mukaisesti kunnan tytäryhteisöjen tilintarkastajat kilpailutetaan siten, että tytäryhteisöissä on kaupungin kanssa sama tilintarkastusyhteisö. Kouvolan kaupunginvaltuusto valitsee tarkastuslautakunnan esityksestä tilintarkastajan Kouvolan kaupungille. Tytäryhteisöt toimivat hankintayksikköinä tilintarkastajiensa valinnassa ja tekevät valintapäätöksen yhtiökokouksessaan. Tarkastettavan kohteen yleiskuvaus Kouvola on n. 78 000 asukkaan kaupunki. Kaupunkikonsernin talouden volyymiä kuvaa vuoden 2025 tilinpäätöksen toimintakulut n. -406 milj. €, toimintakate n. -168 milj. € ja investoinnit n. -84 milj. €. Kaupungin henkilötyövuodet vuonna 2025 on n. 2400 henkilötyövuotta. Kaupungin kirjanpito ja palkanlaskenta on tällä hetkellä ulkoistettu. Yllä esitetyt kohteet ovat esimerkkejä, ja töitä voidaan toteuttaa myös muissa kohteissa. Tarjouspyyntö ei kata kiinteistönomistajan tekemiä/teettämiä muutos- ja korjaustöitä omistamissaan kohteissa, lukuun ottamatta Tampereen korkeakouluyhteisön itse omistamia kiinteistöjä. Muutostyöt kohdistuvat pääsääntöisesti oppimis- ja tutkimusympäristöjen tiloihin, järjestelmiin ja toimintaympäristöihin, niiden käyttäjien tai ylläpidosta vastaavien tahojen tarpeiden perusteella. Yksittäisiä urakkahankintoja koskevat sopimukset voivat olla joko lyhyempiä tai pidempiä kuin varsinainen puitesopimuskausi. Yksittäiset hankintaa koskevat sopimukset voivat tarvittaessa jatkua puitesopimuksen keston yli. Tampereen korkeakoulusäätiö ja Tampereen ammattikorkeakoulu tekevät omat puitesopimuksensa. Project Title: NAMA 326209 EAST POTOMAC SEAWALL DESIGN BUILD Description: NPS requires Design-Build (DB) services for the rehabilitation of approximately 20,700 linear feet of shoreline and seawall infrastructure at East Potomac Park in Washington, DC. The project area includes the shoreline along both the Potomac River and Washington Channel and encompasses associated improvements required to provide long-term shoreline protection, improve drainage performance, preserve public access and protect Park resources. The Contractor shall develop rehabilitation alternatives for NPS evaluation and approval, and implement solutions that satisfy the following project objectives: * Rehabilitate or replace deteriorated shoreline protection infrastructure; * Restore shoreline functionality and reduce impacts associated with daily tidal cycles, minor storm events, erosion, debris loading, ice forces, and long-term settlement; * Evaluate and establish the appropriate historic functional height for shoreline segments within the Park based on historical documentation, engineering analysis, site conditions, and the NPS objectives; * Evaluate opportunities to accommodate future shoreline adaptation measures consistent with NPS planning objectives; * Reuse and repurpose existing seawall materials where feasible and appropriate; * Maintain drainage and flood recovery performance; * Maintain, restore, and develop continuous public access to include Architectural Barriers Act (ABA)-compliant and universal access circulation routes; * Protect existing utilities and adjacent infrastructure; * Preserve historic, cultural, and environmental resources; * Incorporate sustainable, durable, and low operations and maintenance solutions that minimize future operational burden on the NPS. Type of Procurement: Two-Phase Design-Build Selection Procedures (FAR 36.101-2 as deviated). The Government anticipates awarding one firm-fixed price contract for the design and construction services required. One solicitation will be issued with the Phase 1 and Phase 2 requirements. A draft solicitation is attached for review and consideration. Estimated Price Range: More than $10,000,000. Estimated Period of Performance: 51 months after award

USCG - Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has an upcoming requirement to design, build, test, and deliver the Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III). This acquisition recapitalizes the aging fleet of 29-foot Response Boat-Small Second Generation (RB-S II) platforms approaching their end of service life. The contractor will provide the boats, trailers, full logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, and supply support. The RB-S III will be a commercial product designed to execute multiple missions, including Search and Rescue (SAR); Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS); Migrant Interdiction (MI); and Other Law Enforcement (OLE). The Government anticipates procuring up to 400 RB-S III boats for the USCG and an additional 100 modified RB-S III variants for other Federal Government agencies, subject to final requirements, availability of funding, and applicable ordering authority. The Government anticipates awarding up to four (4) Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The resulting delivery orders are anticipated to utilize Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) line items, as identified in the solicitation. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a five (5) year base ordering period and one five (5) year option ordering period. Primary production will take place at the respective contractors' facilities. Delivery will take place at various USCG locations across the continental United States which will be specified in the solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be released by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 26. The Government anticipates providing approximately 45 calendar days for submission of proposals. Formal Question and Answer procedures, including deadline for submission of questions, will be identified in the solicitation. Contract awards are anticipated in the second quarter of FY 2027. The Government anticipates conducting this competitive procurement using a two-phase acquisition methodology: Phase I - Offerors will submit initial technical, management, and conceptual design proposals. The Government will evaluate the Phase I submissions in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and anticipates award of up to four (4) IDIQ contracts. Each IDIQ awardee will proceed to Phase II. Phase II - Each Phase I IDIQ awardee will be issued an initial delivery order satisfying the minimum guarantee under its IDIQ contract to complete the detailed construction/production design, build one (1) demonstration vessel, and participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration. The Government will evaluate the results of each demonstration vessel in accordance with the Phase II evaluation methodology established in the solicitation. Following completion of the Phase II evaluation, the Government anticipates selecting one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive subsequent RB-S III production orders during the remaining ordering period. The final ordering structure and procedures will be established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated solicitation will provide the specific Phase I and Phase II evaluation criteria, evaluation methodology, and basis for selecting the IDIQ contractor anticipated to receive subsequent production orders. title: Cornerstone CS-27-0701 Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology
description: U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Chemical Biological Center (DEVCOM CBC), Rock Island, IL, on behalf of the Office of the Secretary of Defense, Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Industrial Base Policy Innovation Capability and Modernization office via its Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment (IBAS) Program (10 U.S.C. � 4817), in conjunction with Army Contracting Command � Rock Island (ACC-RI), manages the Cornerstone Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022. Cornerstone was architected to create a broad-based, flexible and enduring public-private consortium focused on strategic strengthening of the U.S. Manufacturing and Defense Industrial Base and provide a strong complement to the mandates in Presidential Executive Order 13806. ACC-RI, on behalf of DEVCOM CBC, intends to issue a competitive Cornerstone Initiative Request (CIR) for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology on or after 08 October 2026, with an estimated closing date of 30 calendar days after issuance. The CIR for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology is restricted to Cornerstone consortium members. The CIR will solicit proposals for (1) fixed-price OTA with incremental payments made upon completion of specific milestones. Period of performance will be 36 months. A non-competitive follow-on production OT may be awarded following a successful prototype. The objective of this other transaction prototype project is to design, develop, and demonstrate the Generation 2 (Gen 2) Continuous Feed Narcotics Destruction prototype to modernize and streamline the disposal of seized illicit substances. This effort directly addresses critical logistical bottlenecks, high-maintenance footprints, and security vulnerabilities inherent in legacy batch-feed disposal systems. By transitioning to a high-throughput, continuous-feed technological architecture, this prototype accelerates destruction cycle times, significantly reducing the security risks, costs, and logistical burdens associated with the long-term storage and nationwide transport of seized contraband. Subject to funding, The Cornerstone CIR will solicit prototype fixed-priced proposals for two one Expenditure OTA Agreements with incremental payments made upon completion of specific milestones. The period of performance is estimated to be 36 months. A non-competitive follow-on production OT may be awarded following a successful prototype. Any OT awarded as a result of this initiative will incorporate the following clauses: 1. FAR clause 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment 2. DFARS clause 252.232-7006, WAWF Payment Instructions 3. DFARS clause 252.204-7012, Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting. The CIR is restricted to Cornerstone Consortium members only and will be communicated to the Cornerstone Consortium and companies with pending applications via email. Entities are required to have begun the membership process for their proposal to be reviewed. Entities must have an active registration in SAM.gov, a favorable status in Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information Systems, and be members of the Cornerstone Consortium, with a signed Cornerstone Consortium Management Agreement, to be eligible to submit a proposal and be eligible for awarded this of an OTA task. Contractors may obtain Cornerstone registration information located at https://cornerstone.army.mil or by inquiring at: usarmy.ria.devcom-cbc.mbx.cornerstone-ota@army.mil. Interested parties should stay alert for any changes that may be published to this sam.gov posting. Please email all questions and responses to the following mailbox: usarmy.ria.devcom-cbc.mbx.cornerstone-ota@army.mil This Special Notice is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a CIR or an obligation on behalf of the U.S. Government. Issuance of this Special Notice is not a guarantee of a future CIR or an award and is not a commitment of any kind by the Government.

While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. title: USCG - Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has an upcoming requirement to design, build, test, and deliver the Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III). This acquisition recapitalizes the aging fleet of 29-foot Response Boat-Small Second Generation (RB-S II) platforms approaching their end of service life. The contractor will provide the boats, trailers, full logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, and supply support. The RB-S III will be a commercial product designed to execute multiple missions, including Search and Rescue (SAR); Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS); Migrant Interdiction (MI); and Other Law Enforcement (OLE). The Government anticipates procuring up to 400 RB-S III boats for the USCG and an additional 100 modified RB-S III variants for other Federal Government agencies, subject to final requirements, availability of funding, and applicable ordering authority. The Government anticipates awarding up to four (4) Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The resulting delivery orders are anticipated to utilize Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) line items, as identified in the solicitation. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a five (5) year base ordering period and one five (5) year option ordering period. Primary production will take place at the respective contractors' facilities. Delivery will take place at various USCG locations across the continental United States which will be specified in the solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be released by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 26. The Government anticipates providing approximately 45 calendar days for submission of proposals. Formal Question and Answer procedures, including deadline for submission of questions, will be identified in the solicitation. Contract awards are anticipated in the second quarter of FY 2027. The Government anticipates conducting this competitive procurement using a two-phase acquisition methodology: Phase I - Offerors will submit initial technical, management, and conceptual design proposals. The Government will evaluate the Phase I submissions in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and anticipates award of up to four (4) IDIQ contracts. Each IDIQ awardee will proceed to Phase II. Phase II - Each Phase I IDIQ awardee will be issued an initial delivery order satisfying the minimum guarantee under its IDIQ contract to complete the detailed construction/production design, build one (1) demonstration vessel, and participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration. The Government will evaluate the results of each demonstration vessel in accordance with the Phase II evaluation methodology established in the solicitation. Following completion of the Phase II evaluation, the Government anticipates selecting one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive subsequent RB-S III production orders during the remaining ordering period. The final ordering structure and procedures will be established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated solicitation will provide the specific Phase I and Phase II evaluation criteria, evaluation methodology, and basis for selecting the IDIQ contractor anticipated to receive subsequent production orders. The draft Statement of Work (SOW) and draft Specifications have been attached to this notice as follows: SOW_RB-S_III_Draft Specifications_RB-S_III_Draft /// SPECIAL NOTICE / DISCLAIMER /// This is a Presolicitation Notice only. This is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP). No proposals are being requested, and no contract will be awarded directly from this notice. This notice is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a commitment by the Government to solicit or award a contract for any supply or service. All information contained in this notice, including anticipated quantities, contract structure, ordering periods, acquisition methodology, schedule, technical requirements, and draft documents, is preliminary and subject to change. The draft SOW and draft Specifications are provided for informational purposes and may be revised, replaced, or otherwise modified in the resulting solicitation. The Government may consider feedback, questions, or comments received regarding this notice and the attached draft documents in the development of the resulting solicitation. The Government does not intend to provide individual responses to questions or comments received in response to this notice. Receipt of feedback does not obligate the Government to respond, revise the draft documents, incorporate any recommendations, or otherwise alter the anticipated acquisition. Responses to this notice do not constitute offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any information, documentation, travel, or other costs incurred in connection with this notice. All costs associated with reviewing or responding to this notice are solely at the interested party's expense. The Government reserves the right to modify, delay, cancel, or otherwise determine whether to proceed with this acquisition based on its requirements, acquisition planning, availability of funding, administrative considerations, or other relevant circumstances. Any subsequent solicitation, if issued, will be published on the System for Award Management (SAM.gov). Interested parties are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for any updates, amendments, notices, and any official solicitation associated with this requirement. description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has an upcoming requirement to design, build, test, and deliver the Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III). The contractor will provide the boats, trailers, full logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, and supply support. The RB-S III will be a commercial product designed to execute multiple missions, including Search and Rescue (SAR); Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS); Migrant Interdiction (MI); and Other Law Enforcement (OLE). The Government anticipates procuring up to 400 RB-S III boats for the USCG and an additional 100 modified RB-S III variants for other Federal Government agencies, subject to final requirements, availability of funding, and applicable ordering authority. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a five (5) year base ordering period and one five (5) year option ordering period. Primary production will take place at the respective contractors' facilities. title: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has made a direct award of an definitized single award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract number 693KA8-26-D-00018 to Frequentis USA, Inc, for Digital Remote Towers. This award was made using t
description: Section 161 of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018 laid the groundwork for the development and implementation of remote tower systems (RTSs) to support the modernization of air traffic control services. This initiative aims to explore and deploy RT technology as a cost-effective and efficient alternative to traditional air traffic control towers (ATCTs), particularly in rural and small community airports. The RT program is designed to enhance the FAA's ability to integrate innovative technologies into the National Airspace System (NAS) while maintaining the highest standards of safety and efficiency. RTs provide Visual Flight Rules (VFR) services that extend air traffic control capabilities to underserved areas. The RT program supports the modernization of ATCT infrastructures and promotes cost efficient tower solutions at VFR airports within the (NAS). The program facilitates the evaluation and deployment of RTs, ensuring that they seamlessly transition into real-world operational environments. This initiative supports the FAA's mission to modernize air traffic management and maintain safety and efficiency across the NAS. Under FAA direction and safety oversight, selected airports will integrate and operationalize RT technology, leveraging the insights gained from the System Design Approval (SDA) at the Tech Center. Additional research goals and objectives for government-funded activities may be outlined for sites in specific tasks under the IDIQ. This will help the government evaluate and improve RT technologies in its efforts to continually improve the safety and efficiency of the NAS. This will support the collection and analysis of data essential for: 1. Optimizing RT operations within a multi-runway operational environment. 2. Evaluating the performance and reliability of remote sensing and communication technologies under varied operational conditions. 3. Assessing the infrastructure requirements and scalability of RTS in broader deployment and diverse airport settings. 4. Collecting operational data to inform future policy, safety approvals and implementation decisions. Justification for a Direct Award is summarized as follows: Frequentis (FRQ) is an established global provider of air traffic management and RT solutions. FRQ has deployed digital tower systems internationally and specializes in mission-critical communication and control systems for aviation environments. FRQ has worked in coordination with the FAA and the William J. Hughes Technical Center to develop, and configure, a RTS aligned with FAA safety, human factors, and operational requirements. The FRQ RTS is the only solution that has progressed through the FAA�s SDA process to date. While other vendors offer RT technologies globally, no other system has achieved comparable advancement within the FAA�s design approval and integration framework. Selecting an alternative vendor at this stage would require duplicative design approval activities, additional technical evaluation, and extended safety validation, resulting in significant schedule delays and increased program costs. The program�s reason to establish the RT Program is to comply with Section 621 of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024, which mandates the development and deployment of RT technologies. This initiative aims to enhance air traffic management capabilities at rural and small community airports by integrating advanced RTSs into the NAS. The program is also supporting FAA strategic objectives to modernize the NAS through implementation of innovative, scalable, and cost-effective technologies. RTSs provide a viable alternative to traditional air traffic control infrastructure, enabling expanded service capabilities while optimizing resource utilization across a diverse range of airport environments. Currently, FRQ is the only vendor with a technically acceptable system to comply with the Reauthorization Act of 2024. To meet the requirements, the FAA must leverage the only system that has achieved the necessary level of technical maturity and alignment with FAA standards. While the FAA is actively conducting outreach to additional vendors to participate in the SDA process, onboarding and evaluating alternative systems will require additional time for design approval, testing and validation, and will not support immediate program timelines.

description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. title: CNF INTEGRATED FIRE PROTECTION SYSTEMS
description: CNF Integrated Fire Protection Systems This is a non-personal services contract to support multiple fire protection systems for the Forest Service, Chugach National Forest (CNF), Southcentral Alaska. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn, is responsible to the Government. Purpose: The purpose of this contract is to ensure fire alarm systems, fire suppression systems, backflow preventers, and fire extinguishers are fully functional, compliant with NFPA and OSHA requirements, certified, and ready for emergency use. Description of Services: The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, and all other items and non?personal services necessary to support multiple fire protection systems for the Forest Service, Chugach National Forest, located in Southcentral Alaska. Services include, but are not limited to, inspection, testing, certification, maintenance, installation, repair, replacement, and disposal of fire protection systems and equipment to ensure all units remain safe, compliant, and fully operational. Place of Performance: The work shall be performed at multiple CNF facilities located throughout Southcentral Alaska: Girdwood, Seward, and Cordova. Contract Type: The Government awarded a Firm-Fixed Price, Requirements, Service Contract with up to a 5-Year Ordering Period. description: The California Great Basin Region of the Bureau of Reclamation intends to issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) for a firm fixed-price construction contract for Folsom Dam Vessel Exclusion Barrier and Debris Boom. This procurement will be advertised as a Total Small Business set aside. Solicitation will be issued as an Invitation for Bid (IFB) using FAR Part 14, Sealed Bidding procedures. The work to be performed is described below. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 237990 and the related small business size standard is $45M. This notice is not a request for proposal and the information presented in this announcement will not obligate the Bureau of Reclamation in any manner. All responsible sources may submit a bid which will be considered by the agency. The estimated cost of this project is between $5 Million and $10 Million. This procurement will require 100% performance and payment bonds. The work is located at U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Folsom, California. PRINCIPAL COMPONENTS OF WORK: � Remove and salvage part of the existing barrier on the Folsom dam as shown on the contract drawings. � Design, furnish and install a new vessel exclusion barrier and debris curtain and its components listed on this specification. � Furnish and install onshore anchor on the right-wing side of the dam. � Removal of obstruction along the path of the barrier to the onshore anchor and filling the large gaps on the existing riprap with smaller rocks on the right wing dam. � Furnish and install necessary warning lights and signage. � Design, furnish and installation of necessary anchors, clump anchors, buoys and moorings. � Provide certification of the new barrier according to the requirements set forth on this specification. � Provide one (1) spare module and two (2) spare module-to-module connectors and the required hardware for use. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. Solicitation 140R2026B0001 will be posted electronically via www.sam.gov on or about June 29, 2026. The date for receipt of offers will be approximately July 30, 2026. The solicitation must be downloaded at the above website; no paper copy of this solicitation will be distributed. Prospective contractors MUST be actively registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for award. Questions concerning this solicitation should be directed to Rosana Yousef Goarji via email at rosana_yousefgoarji@ios.doi.gov . This information can be found at: https://www.doi.gov/pam/acquisition/policy/constructioncontract.

title: CNF TRAIL BRUSHING
description: CNF TRAIL BRUSHING This is a non-personal services contract for trail brushing for the Forest Service Chugach National Forest (CNF), Alaska. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn, is responsible to the Government. Purpose: The Forest Service is responsible for maintaining healthy, diverse, and productive National Forests. These responsibilities include maintaining trails and managing vegetation growth. The CNF manages over 500 miles of trails, and the trails identified in the PWS have been designated as current priorities for brushing services. The purpose of this contract is to manage vegetation growth to ensure safe trail conditions and maintain visitor access to National Forest System lands. Description of Services: The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, and all other items and non?personal services necessary to provide brushing services to multiple trails located within the Chugach National Forest. Services shall include cutting, trimming, and disposing of live and dead brush/slash, logs and debris. Place of Performance: The trails covered under this contract are located within the Seward Ranger District (SRD) and Glacier Ranger District (GRD), Chugach National Forest, Alaska. Period of Performance: The period of performance shall be from Date of Award until 30 November 2027. Contract Type: This contract was awarded as a Firm-Fixed Price, Stand-Alone, Non-Personal Services Contract.

description: U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Chemical Biological Center (DEVCOM CBC), Rock Island, IL, on behalf of the Office of the Secretary of Defense, Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Industrial Base Policy Innovation Capability and Modernization office via its Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment (IBAS) Program (10 U.S.C. � 4817), in conjunction with Army Contracting Command � Rock Island (ACC-RI), manages the Cornerstone Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022. Cornerstone was architected to create a broad-based, flexible and enduring public-private consortium focused on strategic strengthening of the U.S. Manufacturing and Defense Industrial Base and provide a strong complement to the mandates in Presidential Executive Order 13806. ACC-RI, on behalf of DEVCOM CBC, intends to issue a competitive Cornerstone Initiative Request (CIR) for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology on or after 08 October 2026, with an estimated closing date of 30 calendar days after issuance. The CIR for Generation 2 Narcotics Destruction Technology is restricted to Cornerstone consortium members. The CIR will solicit white paper proposals for (1) fixed-price OTA with incremental payments made upon completion of specific milestones. Period of performance will be 36 months. A non-competitive follow-on production OT may be awarded following a successful prototype. The objective of this other transaction prototype project is to design, develop, and demonstrate the Generation 2 (Gen 2) Continuous Feed Narcotics Destruction prototype to modernize and streamline the disposal of seized illicit substances. This effort directly addresses critical logistical bottlenecks, high-maintenance footprints, and security vulnerabilities inherent in legacy batch-feed disposal systems. By transitioning to a high-throughput, continuous-feed technological architecture, this prototype accelerates destruction cycle times, significantly reducing the security risks, costs, and logistical burdens associated with the long-term storage and nationwide transport of seized contraband. Any OT awarded as a result of this initiative will incorporate the following clauses: 1. FAR clause 52.204-25, Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment 2. DFARS clause 252.232-7006, WAWF Payment Instructions 3. DFARS clause 252.204-7012, Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting. The CIR is restricted to Cornerstone Consortium members only and will be communicated to the Cornerstone Consortium and companies with pending applications via email. Entities are required to have begun the membership process for their proposal to be reviewed. Entities must have an active registration in SAM.gov, a favorable status in Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information Systems, and be members of the Cornerstone Consortium, with a signed Cornerstone Consortium Management Agreement, to be eligible to submit a proposal and be eligible for awarded this of an OTA task. Contractors may obtain Cornerstone registration information located at https://cornerstone.army.mil or by inquiring at: usarmy.ria.devcom-cbc.mbx.cornerstone-ota@army.mil. Interested parties should stay alert for any changes that may be published to this sam.gov posting. Please email all questions and responses to the following mailbox: usarmy.ria.devcom-cbc.mbx.cornerstone-ota@army.mil This Special Notice is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a CIR or an obligation on behalf of the U.S. Government. title: S208--Landscaping Service Contract
USCG - Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has an upcoming requirement to design, build, test, and deliver the Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III). This acquisition recapitalizes the aging fleet of 29-foot Response Boat-Small Second Generation (RB-S II) platforms approaching their end of service life. The contractor will provide the boats, trailers, full logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, and supply support. The RB-S III will be a commercial product designed to execute multiple missions, including Search and Rescue (SAR); Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS); Migrant Interdiction (MI); and Other Law Enforcement (OLE). The Government anticipates procuring up to 400 RB-S III boats for the USCG and an additional 100 modified RB-S III variants for other Federal Government agencies, subject to final requirements, availability of funding, and applicable ordering authority. The Government anticipates awarding up to four (4) Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The resulting delivery orders are anticipated to utilize Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) line items, as identified in the solicitation. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a five (5) year base ordering period and one five (5) year option ordering period. Primary production will take place at the respective contractors' facilities. Delivery will take place at various USCG locations across the continental United States which will be specified in the solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be released by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 26. The Government anticipates providing approximately 45 calendar days for submission of proposals. Formal Question and Answer procedures, including deadline for submission of questions, will be identified in the solicitation. Contract awards are anticipated in the second quarter of FY 2027. The Government anticipates conducting this competitive procurement using a two-phase acquisition methodology: Phase I - Offerors will submit initial technical, management, and conceptual design proposals. The Government will evaluate the Phase I submissions in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and anticipates award of up to four (4) IDIQ contracts. Each IDIQ awardee will proceed to Phase II. Phase II - Each Phase I IDIQ awardee will be issued an initial delivery order satisfying the minimum guarantee under its IDIQ contract to complete the detailed construction/production design, build one (1) demonstration vessel, and participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration. The Government will evaluate the results of each demonstration vessel in accordance with the Phase II evaluation methodology established in the solicitation. Following completion of the Phase II evaluation, the Government anticipates selecting one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive subsequent RB-S III production orders during the remaining ordering period. The final ordering structure and procedures will be established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated solicitation will provide the specific Phase I and Phase II evaluation criteria, evaluation methodology, and basis for selecting the IDIQ contractor anticipated to receive subsequent production orders. title: Command Wide Broad Agency Announcement for Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center (NAVFAC EXWC) Research, Development, Testing, and Evaluation
description: The primary objective of this work under Solicitation Number N3943026R5001 is to establish a scientifically sound methodology to quantify and evaluate per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) distributions in precipitation, ambient fog water, and ambient soils at multiple active U.S. Navy installations. Ultimately, this study aims to assess how atmospheric deposition (via rain and fog) contributes to PFAS concentrations found in surface soils, and to determine the ideal sample sizes needed to calculate reliable background threshold values (BTVs) for future Navy-wide environmental investigations.

title: FIGHT TONIGHT
description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. S206--Unarmed Security Guard Contract
Construction of a Specialized Mission Training Facility (SMTF), Laurel, MD
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice and not a request for proposals. As such, vendors are not to send capability statements or other such documents. The General Services Administration (GSA) Public Buildings Service (PBS) is seeking a qualified contractor to provide the construction of a Specialized Mission Training Facility (SMTF) in Laurel, MD. Summary: This project includes building the SMTF at the James J. Rowley Training Center (JJRTC), which is the primary training facility for the United States Secret Service (USSS). The training center consists of multiple buildings and structures that provide an environment for various training activities, including active scenario training, as well as classroom and conference room space. Due to increased operational tempo, development of new training programs, and campus population growth in recent years, the USSS continues to develop the JJRTC campus to meet the needs of the USSS mission. To enhance training activities and operational readiness, the USSS intends to construct a full-scale site and building representation of the White House, perimeter buildings, and grounds. Project Scope: The project consists of the work associated with the Site, Center Building, and Perimeter Buildings as described below: Site: The general scope of the project is to replicate (or match) the original building�s grounds on the proposed JJRTC project site. This includes matching both the horizontal and vertical site features of the original grounds. The limits of this replica are the outer curb lines of the proposed perimeter roads (Pennsylvania Avenue, E Street, and West/East Executive Avenue). The scope includes providing stormwater management based on the Maryland Department of the Environment�s (MDE�s) requirements. In addition, existing utilities serving the JJRTC facility will be improved and extended to service the project site. As extensive re-grading will be required, most of the flora and fauna will need to be removed from the site. The proposed replacement flora will include inexpensive, fast-growing, and low-maintenance species. Trees will be matched by general size and either evergreen or deciduous. These types should be selected and placed to match the visual and security functions of the existing trees in the original landscape. Deciduous trees should include shade trees and ornamental (flowering trees). Center Buildings: The Center Buildings are made up of the original building�s 4-story high Main Residence and 3-story high West Wing. Building interiors support multiple training and training support functions. Major building floor areas mirror the original building floor layout, however selected areas designated for dynamic training will be a replica of the original building�s interior conditions without attempting historic and decorative reproduction. Perimeter Buildings: The 18 acres of grounds within the security fence have a series of additional structures that will be recreated for training purposes. Ranging in size and function, additional buildings will be built on the SMTF grounds. The intended project delivery method is a Phased Acquisition procurement using a Two-Phase Construction Concept. The scope of work includes all labor and materials required to provide construction services for the SMTF project pursuant to FAR 15.103 (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-15) and FAR 36 (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-36). The resultant contract will be firm fixed price. The services requested by the contractor shall cover a wide range of construction activities including management, supervision, labor, equipment, and materials required to provide construction and other related services necessary to construct the new facilities. Related services include, but are not limited to, site planning, utilities, testing and inspection during construction, commissioning, and potential additional analysis of the site. The Phase I solicitation is anticipated to be posted on or around March 23, 2026, and the Phase I selection in June of 2026. Phase II solicitation is anticipated to be sent to the shortlisted offerors in July of 2026, with an award anticipated in November of 2026. Currently the substantial completion date is anticipated for 2029. The estimated cost range for construction is between $260,000,000.00 and $290,000,000.00. The total estimated cost of this construction contract is greater than $35 million. As such, in the absence of an exception, this procurement is anticipated to be subject to the Project Labor Agreement requirement in FAR 22.5 (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-22). AMENDMENTS TO SOLICITATION: It is the offeror's responsibility to monitor SAM.gov for the release of any amendments. BONDING: A bid bond is required as well as payment and performance bonds. SECURITY: Before employees are allowed to work under the anticipated contract, all personnel are required to pass a security check. Specific security requirements will be contained in the solicitation. FUNDS AVAILABILITY: Funds are not presently available for this contract. The Government�s obligation under this contract is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. No legal liability on the part of the Government arises until award of the contract. ELIGIBLE OFFERORS: All responsible business firms may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the agency. All prospective offerors are also required to use the System for Award Management at SAM.gov for registering their firm and completing representations and certifications. Prospective offerors shall review the solicitation in detail when it becomes available on www.sam.gov, as items described herein may change.
